title: Add imkarrer/bead-loop to the Buildkite GitHub App, so Buildkite posts commit statuses and the GitHub Action can go
description: You asked to disable the GitHub Action now that Buildkite builds every push and PR. Main's branch protection requires the status context 'ci' (the Action), and Buildkite is not posting any status on bead-loop commits (checked on 10c4ff8: only github-actions' ci) although the pipeline object has publish_commit_status = true — inquire-platform's does post (buildkite/inquire-platform). The difference is the Buildkite GitHub App's repository access: bead-loop is public and not in the App's selected repositories, so Buildkite can only receive the webhook, not write statuses. Human step: github.com/settings/installations → the Buildkite app → add imkarrer/bead-loop. Then I switch main's required check to buildkite/bead-loop and delete .github/workflows/ci.yml (pipeline settings need no change).
acceptance_criteria: A Buildkite status appears on a bead-loop commit; then the workflow is deleted and the required check swapped in one PR.
close_reason: done: the repo was added to the Buildkite GitHub App; buildkite/bead-loop posts on every commit; main's required check is buildkite/bead-loop and .github/workflows/ci.yml is deleted (claude-lane 48dd840). homelab and agent-hub pipelines have the same gap — add them to the App too if their statuses are wanted on GitHub.

title: the page shows decision beads and takes the answer: what the loop (or an agent) asks you, where you look
description: A bead of issue_type 'decision' (or labelled needs-human) in any watched repo is a question for you. status --json gains 'decisions': [{id, title, description, created_at}] per repo (bd list --type decision --status open, plus label needs-human); ui/index.html lists them at the top of Needs you with the description in full and a textarea; bin/bead-loop-ui gets action 'decide' {repo, id, text} that runs 'bd close ID --reason "decided: TEXT"' (the answer is the close reason, where whoever asked reads it); the count in the Needs you heading includes them. Files: src/status.rs, ui/index.html, bin/bead-loop-ui, test/run.sh (the status_json_and_ui case), test/ui-onclicks.js (lever 'decide').
acceptance_criteria: A decision bead in the fixture appears under Needs you with its text; POST /api/decide closes it with the reason; the onclick check passes; README's Watching it names it.
close_reason: shipped in PR #35: status --json carries 'decisions' (open beads of type decision or labelled needs-human); the page lists them first under Needs you with the text in full and Answer & close (POST /api/decide → bd close --reason 'decided: …' and the bell); the suite covers it.

title: Deploy via flox: a tree environment on this box, or a published package pulled by generation?
description: Today deploy is git pull + cargo build --release on this box (bead-loop-deploy.timer, ~2-3 min cold). Two flox shapes, both already in the homelab: (a) TREE — the units run 'flox activate -d ~/src/bead-loop -- bead-supervisor run' off the live checkout, the binary built there by 'flox build' from a [build] table; no catalog, no signing, deploy stays a pull. (b) PACKAGE — CI does 'flox build' + 'flox publish' to the Flox catalog on green (needs a catalog org and a signing key), the box pulls a generation like agent-hub's floxhub kind and never runs cargo. (a) is a day and needs nothing from you; (b) is cleaner and needs: which catalog org, where the signing key lives, and whether the workstation may pull from FloxHub unattended.
acceptance_criteria: An answer choosing (a) or (b); for (b) the org name and where the key goes. The floxify beads then unblock.
close_reason: decided: (b) — a published flox package on the Flox catalog, built and published by CI on green, pulled by generation on the workstation; cargo leaves the box. bl-s89 unblocks; bl-cyx (the [build] table) is its first step.

title: notify: post to the channel of your choice when a bead needs you, Claude signs out, or the loop goes down
description: After the decision on where (see the decision bead). src/notify.rs: notify(kind, text) reads 'notify' from the global config (ntfy://topic or a webhook url), POSTs through curl (the stub in test/bin records it), never blocks a round. Callers: send_back when it parks, hold (once per reason), the merge watcher's holds, claude_ok turning false, recover at start ('the loop is back'). A daily digest of Needs you at 'notify_digest = "09:00"'. The page shows the channel and the last post. README: the Config table and Watching it.
acceptance_criteria: test/run.sh: parking a bead posts once (the stub curl log has the topic and the text); a hold posts once per reason; a second pass posts nothing; no 'notify' key posts nothing. Documented.
close_reason: not wanted: the human is told in the UI, not by a channel (bl-st2). The page's Needs you with a clear question/reason is bl-s8k.

title: Where should the loop tell you it needs you? (ntfy topic / Discord webhook / nothing)
description: The loop parks and holds beads for you and shows them on the page — but nothing reaches you when you are not looking at it. The homelab bot already posts to a Discord status channel and an ntfy topic. Which of those (or which other channel) should the loop use, and for what: every bead entering Needs you; Claude signing out; the loop going down; a daily digest at a time you name? Answer with the channel and its address (an ntfy topic name, or where the Discord webhook url lives — a sops secret, ~/.config/bead-loop/notify?).
acceptance_criteria: An answer on this bead naming the channel(s), the address, and the events; the notifications bead then unblocks.
close_reason: decided: the page is the channel — no ntfy/Discord. What is missing is not delivery but the question: Needs you must show WHY (the question or reason) for every entry, and decision beads must appear there with their text. That is bl-s8k, now P1.

title: lanes per model server: acbox worker rounds and acbox reviews stop colliding
description: The Claude lane is the first lane per server. Generalize per docs/design-lanes-per-server.md: one lane per provider named in the stages (devbox, acbox, claude), each taking any queued round — a worker round for a ready bead, a reviewer round for a bead in review — whose model's provider is its own; review rounds before dev rounds, then fewest failures. pause/resume take a provider. status --json lanes keyed by provider (the page's lane panels follow). The dev/review pair remains the shape when no [[stages]] table names more than one provider.
acceptance_criteria: The lane cases in test/run.sh rewritten for 'stub' as a provider; a case shows an acbox review waiting while an acbox worker round runs and a devbox round proceeding meanwhile; the page shows one panel per provider.

title: Claude lane parallelism (after the decision): claude_parallel = N
description: Blocked on the Claude-parallelism decision. The claude lane runs up to N rounds at once (threads), each with its own lane marker lane.claude.1..N; picks exclude beads on any of them; the page shows N panels or one panel with N rows.
acceptance_criteria: With claude_parallel = 2 and two Claude-stage beads, both rounds run at once (two stub claude calls with overlapping timestamps in the fixture); default 1 behaves as today.
close_reason: moot: the decision is one at a time (bl-a5v)

title: the units run inside the flox environment: the runtime deps come from the manifest, not the login profile
description: systemd/*.service ExecStart become 'flox activate -d %h/src/bead-loop -- <command>' (bead-supervisor run; bin/bead-loop-ui; opencode web) so bd, gh, opencode, node, curl and the binary resolve from .flox/env/manifest.toml on every box the same way, and PATH= lines go. install.sh unchanged otherwise; scripts/deploy.sh restarts them as now. Check flox activate's startup cost on a warm env (should be under a second) and note it.
acceptance_criteria: After install.sh the three units start and 'systemctl --user show -p Environment' carries no PATH= line; the loop works a stub bead end to end; documented in README's Layout.

title: publish on green and deploy by generation (if the flox decision is PACKAGE)
description: Blocked on the deploy-via-flox decision choosing (b). CI's main build: flox build + flox publish -o <org> bead-supervisor (signing key from the agent's secrets); the workstation: a flox environment that installs <org>/bead-supervisor, bead-loop-deploy.timer becomes 'flox pull/upgrade' of that env and a restart, with the generation recorded like homelab's environment-pull writes its pin; cargo leaves the workstation.
acceptance_criteria: A merge to main lands on the box as a new generation within two minutes with no cargo run; hub-status-style line says which generation is applied.

title: deploy the binary CI built instead of rebuilding it on this box
description: scripts/deploy.sh runs cargo build --release on the workstation (2-3 min, the GPU box's CPU). The main build on ac-box already built it: upload target/release/bead-supervisor as a Buildkite artifact in the rust step on main (buildkite-agent artifact upload), and let deploy.sh fetch the newest passed main build's artifact through the Buildkite API (the homelab token via scripts/lib/buildkite-token.sh) when the commit matches origin/main, falling back to cargo build when it does not. Superseded by the flox PACKAGE shape if that decision goes (b).
acceptance_criteria: A merge to main deploys within two minutes without cargo running on the box (journal of bead-loop-deploy.service shows 'artifact <sha>'); a build the API cannot serve falls back to cargo; README's deploy paragraph updated.

title: flox [build] for bead-supervisor: the binary as a flox package from this checkout
description: .flox/env/manifest.toml gains [build.bead-supervisor] with command = 'cargo build --release && mkdir -p $out/bin && cp target/release/bead-supervisor $out/bin/' (flox 1.16 build table), so 'flox build bead-supervisor' produces result-bead-supervisor/bin/bead-supervisor. scripts/ci.sh rust runs 'flox build' too when flox is present (it is on the agent). install.sh prefers the flox build's output. README: Layout and Checks.
acceptance_criteria: 'flox build bead-supervisor' in this checkout yields a binary that passes 'SUP=result-bead-supervisor/bin/bead-supervisor test/run.sh'; CI's rust step logs the build; install.sh installs from it when present.

title: test/run.sh in parallel: the suite in a quarter of the time
description: Every case is isolated in its own mktemp dir, so run them concurrently: test/run.sh takes -j N (default nproc/2), runs cases through xargs -P with each case's output to its own file, prints them in order, keeps the pass/fail totals and the exit code. The UI case binds a random port already; the lock_skips and sigterm cases use per-fixture paths. The gate and CI use the default.
acceptance_criteria: 'test/run.sh' on this box finishes in under 20 s with the same pass count; '-j 1' is today's behaviour; a failing case still fails the run with its FAIL lines.

title: a provider's server down holds the lane, not each bead in turn
description: When devbox or acbox is unreachable every bead the lane picks is held one by one, five minutes apart, each with a note. Instead: server_ok(provider) beside claude_ok in src/harness.rs — GET the provider's baseURL/models (from opencode.json), cached 60 s, forgotten on wake — and pick_runnable treats a round whose server is down like a signed-out Claude round: skipped with one log line per pass ('N bead(s) wait for devbox — its server is not answering'), no hold, no note. status --json gains 'servers': {provider: ok} and the page shows a banner per server, like Claude's.
acceptance_criteria: test/bin gets a stub curl route for /models controlled by TEST_CTRL/server-down.<provider>; with it set no round runs and no bead is held or noted; cleared, the next pass runs; the page shows the banner.

title: bead-supervisor doctor: every dependency probed, red or green, in one command
description: src/doctor.rs: bd (version), git, gh auth status, claude auth status, each opencode provider named in the stages (GET baseURL/models from opencode.json, 5 s), the attach server (GET /session), disk free under the state dir, the three units' state when systemctl exists. Text with one line per probe; --json for the page. bin/bead-loop-ui runs it once a minute and shows a banner for anything red (replacing the Claude-only banner). README: Run.
acceptance_criteria: 'bead-supervisor doctor' exits 1 with a red line when the stub 'claude auth status' says signed out and 0 when all green; --json is an array of {name, ok, detail}; the page banner case in test/run.sh covers one red probe.

title: Claude lane: one round at a time, or several in parallel?
description: The Claude lane runs one claude/* round at a time. Anthropic can run many; local models cannot. With repeat and two beads stuck on Claude today, parallel Claude rounds would clear them together. Cost is the only reason not to. Say a number (1, 2, 4) — and whether the loop should refuse to start a Claude round when the day's spend passes a figure.
acceptance_criteria: An answer with the parallelism and any spend cap; a bead 'claude_parallel = N' follows.
close_reason: decided: one Claude round at a time, with the same priority-queue semantics as every lane (no open blocker, fewest failures first, then bd's order). No spend cap. bl-vg2 is moot.

title: close a bead whose bead/<id> PR merged outside the loop
description: reconcile only looks at PRs it opened or adopted while open, so a bead worked by hand or by a subagent — its PR on branch bead/<id> merged before the loop saw it — stays open and the dev queue would work it again (this happened on 2026-09-20 for six beads: bl-568, bl-xkm, bl-1zx, bl-6e0, bl-czd, bl-ti0). In bin/bead-supervisor reconcile, after adopt: for each open bead the label names (bdr ready -l LABEL) that has no inflight marker, no review marker and no worktree, ask 'gh pr list --state merged --head bead/ID --json url,mergedAt --jq .[0]' (one call per such bead; cache nothing — the dev queue is short); when a merged PR exists, close the bead with reason 'bead-loop: <url> merged outside the loop' and log it. Adopted-style slugs (bead/ID-slug) count too: use --search 'head:bead/ID' if --head is exact-match only, and verify with the stub gh's list contract. Files: bin/bead-supervisor (reconcile), test/bin/gh (pr list --state merged), test/run.sh (a case: a bead open, a merged PR planted in extra-prs.json with state MERGED and headRefName bead/t-1 → sup reconcile closes t-1 with the url in the reason; a bead with an open PR is not touched), README outcome table (one row).
acceptance_criteria: The new case passes; every existing case passes; shellcheck clean.

title: wire the second-family reviewer and the utility model into the stages, the opencode provider, and the README
description:
Follows homelab-e00 (a non-Qwen reviewer resident on ac-box, trial gpt-oss-120b) and homelab-8r5 (a small utility model there). Nothing in bead-loop discovers models: they are named in three places that all need the new entries once the backends exist on :8100.

1. ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json, provider acbox.models: add the reviewer (tool_call true, limit.context 32768, output 8192) and the utility model; point small_model at acbox/<utility> so opencode's titles and summaries stop landing on an 80B slot. The live loop reads the global config, so this is the change that takes effect.
2. ~/.config/bead-loop/config.toml stages: stage 1 reviewer stays acbox/coder or moves to acbox/<reviewer> (decide from the e00 side-by-side notes); stage 2 (worker acbox/coder) reviewer becomes acbox/<reviewer> instead of acbox/instruct -- that is the pair the different-family rule is for. Keep failures counts.
3. agents/bead-reviewer.md: 'model: acbox/coder' is the default the stage table overrides -- update the comment/default if the reviewer moves; if the chosen model takes a reasoning-effort field (gpt-oss does), decide the level for reviews and set it in the provider options.
4. bead-loop.example.toml and README's stage table, the model-server diagram (README line ~43 names acbox/coder as the reviewer box) and the 'Why this shape' bullet: name the new reviewer and the reason (a different lineage checking the Qwen worker).
5. Watch the first five reviews through the new stage in logs/*.review.jsonl: step tok/s, REJECT/APPROVE shape parses (the supervisor keys on the leading REJECT:/APPROVE: -- a model that prefixes reasoning or markdown breaks it; test before switching).
acceptance_criteria: A bead reaching stage 2 is reviewed by acbox/<reviewer> (log line names it); a stage-1 review still passes; opencode small_model calls hit the utility backend (its /metrics counters move); README and example config name the models and the reason.
notes: Blocked on homelab-e00 (reviewer) and homelab-8r5 (utility model) in ~/src/homelab -- cross-repo, so not a bd dep; do not start until both backends answer on :8100/running.

title: Buildkite pipeline through the flox plugin, on queue self
description: Add .buildkite/pipeline.yml: every step runs inside this repo's .flox/ through the imkarrer/flox plugin (ref main, as inquire-platform's pipeline does and for the same reason: the tagged hooks begin #!/bin/bash, which NixOS lacks), on agents with queue=self. Steps, each with a timeout of 10 minutes or less: (1) syntax + shellcheck: 'bash -n bin/bead-supervisor install.sh test/run.sh test/lint-skills.sh test/bin/* && node --check bin/bead-loop-ui && shellcheck -S warning bin/bead-supervisor install.sh test/run.sh test/lint-skills.sh test/bin/*'; (2) 'test/lint-skills.sh'; (3) 'test/run.sh' (15 minutes; it takes ~5). Steps 2 and 3 wait for step 1. Add shellcheck to .flox/env/manifest.toml [install] if it is not there (it is: check). README 'Checks' section: one sentence saying the same checks run on Buildkite through the plugin and on GitHub Actions. Files: .buildkite/pipeline.yml (new), README.md.
acceptance_criteria: The file parses as YAML ('yq -p yaml . .buildkite/pipeline.yml' exits 0); it names plugin imkarrer/flox#main on every step and agents queue self; every step has a timeout_in_minutes; README mentions Buildkite in Checks. (The pipeline itself is created in Buildkite by the operator, pointing at this repo; that is not part of this bead.)

title: aider as a worker harness: worker = "aider:<provider>/<model>"
description: In bin/bead-supervisor run_agent, add a case for models named 'aider:PROVIDER/MODEL' (e.g. aider:devbox/coder): run aider non-interactively in the worktree — 'aider --yes-always --no-auto-commits --no-gitignore --model openai/MODEL --message "$prompt" FILES', with OPENAI_API_BASE taken from the opencode provider's baseURL in ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json (jq .provider[PROVIDER].options.baseURL) and OPENAI_API_KEY set to a dummy when unset, --lint-cmd "$GATE" when GATE is set, and FILES = the paths the bead's DESCRIPTION names (every whitespace-separated token containing a slash or a dot that exists in the worktree; the workflow skill already requires the description to name its files). Aider's stdout is the log (same $logf); the round's 'final' text is the last 20 lines. The worker's DONE:/BLOCKED: protocol does not apply to aider: treat a non-zero exit as failure, a zero exit with a commit-able diff as DONE (settle_worktree commits it). The reviewer harness is unchanged (aider does not review). Document in README (Config table: model naming; a paragraph 'Harnesses' under 'Why this shape' stating when aider is the better choice — small model, file-scoped bead, runnable gate — and when opencode is) and in bead-loop.example.toml. Add test/bin/aider (a stub with the same $TEST_CTRL contract: records its args and files to calls, edits work.txt) and a case in test/run.sh: a stage with worker aider:stub/worker works a bead whose description names work.txt; the stub aider is called with work.txt, --lint-cmd true, --model openai/worker; the round reaches review and a PR.
acceptance_criteria: test/run.sh passes including the new case; shellcheck clean; README and the example toml name the aider: form.

title: measure the CI cache: cold vs warm rust step on ac-box, and what to do if warm is still slow
description: Build #1 (cold: toolchain + registry + full compile) vs #2+ (warm target dir beside the checkouts). Record both in docs/design-resident-loop.md or a docs/ci.md. If the warm rust step is over 3 min, split fmt+clippy from build+test as two parallel steps, or add sccache to the flox env with its cache beside the target dir.
acceptance_criteria: The two durations are in docs with the build numbers; a change if warranted.

title: held: back off exponentially, and park after a day
description: A hold is retried every 5 min (BEAD_LOOP_HOLD_BACKOFF). Make it 5, 10, 20, 40, 60 min (cap) from the hold's age and a count kept in held/ID.n, and after 24 h held with the same reason, park the bead with the reason (the human queue proper). src/round.rs hold_expired, src/state.rs; status shows the next retry.
acceptance_criteria: test/run.sh: with BEAD_LOOP_HOLD_BACKOFF=1 a bead held twice is skipped at 1 s and picked at 2 s; a hold with mtime 25 h old is parked on the next pass with its reason in the note.

title: the page shows what the worker is doing now: the session's last lines under the lane
description: Under each busy lane panel, the last 5 tool calls / text lines of the live session (what 'bead-supervisor log' prints), refreshed with the state push. Source: the opencode server's session messages (GET /session/ID/message) when attach is set; the claude -p log file otherwise. bin/bead-loop-ui fetches per busy lane, bounded; ui/index.html renders a small mono block.
acceptance_criteria: With a stub session in the fixture the lane panel shows the lines; no attach shows nothing; the page's script still parses.

title: UI: a Claude column — every bead on the claude/* stage and where it sits
description: In ui/index.html, add a fourth queue column after merge, titled 'Claude' (colour: var(--blue)), listing every bead whose current stage (b.stage) names a claude/* worker or reviewer — drawn from queues.dev, queues.review and the lanes — with where it sits (dev queue #n, review queue #n, on the dev/review lane) and its failures chip; empty state 'no bead on the Claude stage'. Subtitle: 'the last stage; runs on the dev and review lanes'. It is a view over the other queues, not new state: status --json does not change. Keep the grid readable: .queues becomes four columns at width, stacking to one below 1000px. Files: ui/index.html only.
acceptance_criteria: The page's script parses (node --check on the extracted script); with the fixture in case_status_json_and_ui plus one bead whose stage is claude/*, the rendered page (test/render via the existing render-test harness pattern, or a small assertion added to the UI case fetching the page and checking the column header exists) shows a 'Claude' column; the existing UI case still passes.

title: UI: a bead's round history behind an expander
description: status --json: every bead entry (queues.dev, queues.review, lanes, parked) gets 'history': the lines of failures/ID.notes as an array of strings (empty when the file is absent) — in bin/bead-supervisor status_json, read once per bead id. ui/index.html: any bead row with failures > 0 gets a small '▸ N rounds' toggle that expands to list the history lines in order (round N (model): note…), monospace, muted; collapsed by default; no re-render flicker (keep the open/closed state in a Set keyed by bead id across renders). Files: bin/bead-supervisor (status_json only), ui/index.html.
acceptance_criteria: In case_status_json_and_ui, a bead with a failures/ID.notes of two lines has .history of length 2 in --json status; the page's script parses; existing cases pass; shellcheck clean.

title: bead-level harness override: label harness:opencode or harness:aider
description: In bin/bead-supervisor dev_one, after stage_for picks S_MODEL: if the bead's labels (bd show --json .[0].labels) include 'harness:opencode', strip an 'aider:' prefix from the worker model; if they include 'harness:aider' and the model has no prefix and is not claude/*, add 'aider:'. Log which harness was chosen and why when a label changed it. README: one paragraph under 'Harnesses' describing the labels. Depends on the aider harness bead.
acceptance_criteria: A case in test/run.sh: a stage with worker aider:stub/worker and a bead labelled harness:opencode is worked by the opencode stub (calls shows bead-worker via opencode, not aider); the reverse (stub/worker + harness:aider) runs the aider stub.

title: rust: the UI server inside the binary; cutover; retire the bash
description: Port bin/bead-loop-ui (state, SSE, the levers, PR cache, claude auth, login flow) into the binary as 'bead-supervisor ui' serving ui/index.html unchanged (rust/src/ui.rs; a small HTTP dependency is acceptable here, e.g. tiny_http or axum — one, justified in the commit). systemd/bead-loop-ui.service runs 'bead-supervisor ui'. install.sh builds (cargo build --release) and links the binary; .flox/env/manifest.toml gets cargo; CI builds and runs the suite against the binary; bin/bead-supervisor and bin/bead-loop-ui are removed; README's Layout and Checks sections updated.
acceptance_criteria: test/run.sh passes with SUP pointing at the release binary and the UI case talking to 'bead-supervisor ui'; CI green; the bash scripts are gone from the tree.
notes: rescoped after #33: the bash is gone; what remains is porting bin/bead-loop-ui (node) into the binary as 'bead-supervisor ui' — SSE, the levers, PR cache, claude login flow — with ui/index.html served unchanged. Not urgent: the node server works and is 300 lines.

title: rust: lanes per model server, replacing lane dev|review
description: Per docs/design-lanes-per-server.md 'Lanes per server': a tick starts one lane per provider named in the stages (devbox, acbox, claude); each lane takes any queued round — a worker round for a ready bead, a reviewer round for a bead in review — whose model's provider is its own, review rounds before dev rounds, then fewest failures, then bd's order; leaves after the others have looked idle three checks running. pause/resume take a server name. lane.<server> holds bead and role. rust/src/lane.rs, rust/src/tick.rs. Rewrite the lane cases in test/run.sh (lanes_run_side_by_side, review_lane_waits_for_dev_to_claim, pause_one_lane, tick_goes_round_while_there_is_work) for 'stub' as the server name; the UI's lane panels become one per server (ui/index.html lanePanel).

title: Rust rewrite of the supervisor: same CLI, same state, same tests
description: bin/bead-supervisor is ~1000 lines of bash gluing bd, gh, git, opencode, jq and curl. Two of today's bugs were bash bugs (an apostrophe in a ${x:+…} word emptied every worker prompt; 'claude auth status' exit codes). The lanes-per-server change (docs/design-lanes-per-server.md) is a rewrite of the core anyway. Rewrite the supervisor in Rust as one binary, bead-supervisor, with the SAME command-line surface, the same state on disk (~/.local/state/bead-loop/<repo>/…), the same config (TOML), the same agents/skills/UI page and systemd units. test/run.sh with its stub CLIs (test/bin) is the acceptance spec: the binary is done when every case passes against it unchanged. Children of this epic are worked in order; none is worked until the dogfood loop is running on this repo.
acceptance_criteria: All of test/run.sh passes against the Rust binary with no change to the tests or stubs; install.sh links the binary; the bash script is removed.
